_about: Antonio de Guaras, London, 14 June 1574 (TNA SP 70/131 ff. 109r-110r; CSP Foreign 1572-74 no. 1452). One-to-one substitution, cipher sign -> plain letter, rebuilt by AI agents and matched against the plain text printed by Kervyn de Lettenhove (1888), vol. VII pp. 176-178. Sign names as in transcription_full_ai_reading.txt. 'status': swap = one of the seven reciprocal neighbour swaps; forced = fixed by the words of the text; not_forced = the value is arbitrary.

8.words: tanbien, parte (the only two sure places, both at a line start); 8 may be a second sign for t beside s, perhaps a capital or initial form of it; the frozen key of the first test had z here, corrected after the test, and the test sample has no 8

l.words: occurs only as 'l' with a raised p before a dot, an abbreviation ending (her[man]o, seru[ici]o, neg[oci]o, prim[o]); 'y' is an arbitrary value

marks.^2: raised sign like a small 2: abbreviation mark, no letter value
marks.^p: raised p after l: abbreviation ending, no letter value
